title: Development for Roadway Infrastructure Improvements
short_description: RFPQ for multidisciplinary development and construction support for city roadway improvements.
project_scope: Citywide transportation and roadway infrastructure improvements within the City of La Porte. The notice indicates a broad, multidisciplinary program covering roadway-related development and construction, but provides no technical parameters such as bridge types, spans, lengths, lane configurations, or construction quantities.
services: Multidisciplinary services requested: landscape architecture, civil engineering, geotechnical engineering, surveying/GIS/mapping, construction/project management, environmental engineering/planning/design, structural engineering, utility engineering, and transportation planning.
relevance_explanation:
- Broad roadway infrastructure program with no defined bridge or special structural scope.
- Includes structural engineering, but this appears to be one discipline among many in a general streets/highways procurement.
- Likely focused on roadway and municipal infrastructure rather than architecturally or structurally demanding structures.
- Also includes several low-priority disciplines for sbp such as project management, surveying, geotechnics, and environmental planning.
- No evidence of large spans, innovative structures, sustainability focus, or a clear planning role for complex load-bearing structures.
construction_cost_explanation: No construction budget is stated in the notice. The source only describes a general RFPQ for roadway infrastructure improvements and provides no quantities, limits, technical scope, or funding information, so a realistic cost estimate is not possible.
fee_explanation: No fee information is provided. Because the notice is a broad multidisciplinary RFPQ without defined structural scope, contract value, or service extent, a realistic sbp fee estimate is not possible.
references_qualifications: Qualified firms are sought for roadway infrastructure development and construction. Requested disciplines include landscape architecture, civil engineering, geotechnical engineering, surveying/GIS/mapping, construction/project management, environmental engineering/planning/design, structural engineering, utility engineering, and transportation planning. No specific minimum reference counts or qualification thresholds are stated in the source.
